---
title: Build a connector
description: Make a connector with the connector kit, run it against a stand-in ticket service, and see the items it writes to your instance.
---

- **You'll build** a connector for a small ticket service. It reads the tickets an account holds and writes each one to your instance as an item.
- **You need** your own Marfa instance **on the computer you work on**, with the CLI signed in to it, as the [Quickstart](/quickstart) leaves you. You also need Git, [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22.13 or later and [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/installation) 11.
- **You'll have** a connector that runs once against the service and leaves two tickets in your instance.

A connector reads a vendor, the service that holds the records, and writes what it finds as items. The connector kit registers the connector, writes only what changed and reports each run, so your code only reads the vendor. [Connectors](/build/connectors) explains the parts, and the [kit's README](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa-connectors/blob/main/template/README.md) is its reference.

**A connector's key can be made only on the server's own computer**, through its private socket, because the kit refuses a key made under the CLI's sign-in. An instance on Railway has no way to make one today, so this tutorial needs an instance on your own computer.

<Steps paged>
<Step>

### Get the kit

The [marfa-connectors](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa-connectors) repository holds the connector kit, `@withmarfa/connector`, a template, and the connectors Marfa ships. The kit isn't published to npm, so build it from the repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa-connectors.git
cd marfa-connectors
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build
```

Keep this folder as your working folder for the rest of the tutorial.

</Step>
<Step>

### Make a ticket service

Here the vendor is a stand-in that serves a list from a file, so you can change the list later and watch the connector follow. In a second terminal, make a folder outside the checkout, such as `ticket-service`, and save the list in it:

```json title="ticket-service/tickets.json"
[
  { "id": "T-1041", "event": "Khruangbin", "venue": "Roundhouse, London", "starts": "2026-12-04T19:30:00Z" },
  { "id": "T-1187", "event": "Nils Frahm", "venue": "Barbican Hall, London", "starts": "2027-01-15T20:00:00Z" }
]
```

Save the service beside it. It answers `GET /tickets` with the account's name and its tickets, and only for the token `demo-token-1234`:

```js title="ticket-service/service.mjs"
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

createServer(async (request, response) => {
  if (request.headers.authorization !== "Bearer demo-token-1234") {
    response.writeHead(401).end();
  } else if (request.url === "/tickets") {
    const tickets = JSON.parse(await readFile("tickets.json", "utf8"));
    response.writeHead(200, { "Content-Type": "application/json" });
    response.end(JSON.stringify({ account: "sam", tickets }));
  } else {
    response.writeHead(404).end();
  }
}).listen(4100, "127.0.0.1", () => {
  console.log("Your tickets are at http://127.0.0.1:4100");
});
```

Start it, and leave it running:

<Terminal>

```bash
cd ticket-service
node service.mjs
```

```text
Your tickets are at http://127.0.0.1:4100
```

</Terminal>

</Step>
<Step>

### Start the connector and describe its type

Back in `marfa-connectors`, make a folder for the connector from the template's package files:

```bash
mkdir -p connectors/tickets/src
cp template/connector/package.json template/connector/tsconfig.json connectors/tickets/
```

In `connectors/tickets/package.json`, change `"name": "example"` to `"name": "tickets"`.

Each ticket becomes an item of a type the connector registers. A type names its fields; this one extends `core.event`, which already has a `title`, a `place` and a `starts_at`, and adds the vendor's ticket number:

```json title="connectors/tickets/src/tickets.ticket.json"
{
  "id": "tickets.ticket",
  "label": "Ticket",
  "description": "A ticket from the ticket service, for the event it admits you to.",
  "parent": "core.event",
  "fields": {
    "ticket_id": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "The ticket's number in the ticket service." }
  },
  "display_hints": { "icon": "lucide:ticket" }
}
```

[Items and types](/build/items-and-types) explains types and their parents.

</Step>
<Step>

### Read the service

Keep the vendor's own API in a file of its own. This one fetches the tickets and stops if the service refuses:

```ts title="connectors/tickets/src/service.ts"
export interface Ticket { id: string; event: string; venue?: string; starts: string }

export async function readTickets(address: string, token: string, signal: AbortSignal) {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("tickets", `${address}/`), {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
    signal: AbortSignal.any([signal, AbortSignal.timeout(30_000)]),
  });
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`the ticket service answered ${String(response.status)}`);
  }
  return (await response.json()) as { account: string; tickets: Ticket[] };
}
```

An error thrown here fails the run, and the kit reports it with this message.

</Step>
<Step>

### Write the connector

`defineConnector` says what the connector is, and `run` turns each ticket into an entry:

```ts title="connectors/tickets/src/main.ts"
import { defineConnector, main, type TypeDefinition } from "@withmarfa/connector";
import ticketType from "./tickets.ticket.json" with { type: "json" };
import { readTickets } from "./service.js";

const connector = defineConnector({
  name: "tickets",
  description: "The tickets you hold in the ticket service.",
  source: "tickets",
  sourceName: "Tickets",
  types: [{ type: ticketType as TypeDefinition, fields: ["ticket_id", "title", "place", "starts_at"] }],
  env: { TICKETS_URL: "required", TICKETS_TOKEN: "secret" },
  async run({ env, signal, upsert }) {
    const { account, tickets } = await readTickets(env.TICKETS_URL, env.TICKETS_TOKEN, signal);
    await upsert(ticketType.id, tickets.map((ticket) => ({
      source_id: `${account}:${ticket.id}`,
      properties: { ticket_id: ticket.id, title: ticket.event, place: ticket.venue, starts_at: ticket.starts },
      occurred_at: ticket.starts,
    })));
  },
});

await main(connector);
```

- **`source`** is the code every item the connector writes carries. It names the system the items come from, never an account. **`sourceName`** is how Marfa shows it; the kit sets it on the first start and keeps a name the owner gives it later.
- **`source_id`** is the vendor's ID for the record. With the source, it is the item's natural key, so the next run finds and updates the item instead of writing a second one. A ticket belongs to an account, so its ID starts with the account.
- **`env`** names the settings the connector reads. The kit stops the start if one is missing, and never writes a `secret` to its log.

Install and build it:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm exec tsc -b connectors/tickets
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Make its key and run it

A connector gets a key of its own, which reaches its own type and nothing else. Make it through the server's private socket, `data/control/marfa.sock` in the folder `marfa server status` prints, `~/marfa-server` by default. A key made under the CLI's sign-in belongs to that sign-in, and the kit refuses it.

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa --socket ~/marfa-server/data/control/marfa.sock keys create \
  --label "Ticket connector" --source tickets \
  --type-permission tickets.ticket=write \
  --metadata-permission types=write --default-tier feed
```

```text
marfa_k1_…
key 01a1f16f-80ae-7481-b843-1db25e64b513 (Ticket connector); the plaintext is shown once, keep it now
  tickets.ticket     Read and edit
  Custom data types  Read and edit
```

</Terminal>

<Callout type="warn" title="Copy the key now">Marfa shows it once. If you lose it, revoke it with `marfa keys revoke` and make another.</Callout>

`--source` makes the key write under `tickets`, and `types=write` lets the connector register its type. Run the connector once with the key and the service's settings, replacing `<connector key>` with the key and the address with your instance's:

<Terminal>

```bash
MARFA_API_URL=http://localhost:8600 MARFA_API_KEY=<connector key> \
  TICKETS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4100 TICKETS_TOKEN=demo-token-1234 \
  node connectors/tickets/dist/main.js --once
```

```text
2026-11-19T01:33:06.017Z info registered as 01a1f16f-9c3d-7407-91a3-a55d024651ea
2026-11-19T01:33:06.064Z info run succeeded: created 2, updated 0, archived 0, unchanged 0, skipped 0
```

</Terminal>

On its first start the kit checks the key, registers the connector and its type, and then runs.

</Step>
<Step>

### See what it wrote

List the tickets with your own CLI:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa items list --type tickets.ticket
```

```text
id                                    type            when                      title
01a1f16f-9c7d-733a-ba51-db13974977de  tickets.ticket  2027-01-15T20:00:00.000Z  Nils Frahm
01a1f16f-9c7c-74ba-ac82-919ada1113f9  tickets.ticket  2026-12-04T19:30:00.000Z  Khruangbin
```

</Terminal>

Read one in full, using an ID from your own list:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa items get 01a1f16f-9c7c-74ba-ac82-919ada1113f9 --json
```

```json
{
  "item": {
    "id": "01a1f16f-9c7c-74ba-ac82-919ada1113f9",
    "type": "tickets.ticket",
    "state": "active",
    "tier": "feed",
    "occurred_at": "2026-12-04T19:30:00.000Z",
    "source": "tickets",
    "source_id": "sam:T-1041",
    "version": 1,
    "read_only": true,
    "properties": {
      "title": "Khruangbin",
      "starts_at": "2026-12-04T19:30:00Z",
      "place": "Roundhouse, London",
      "ticket_id": "T-1041"
    }
  }
}
```

</Terminal>

The answer has more fields than this. The item waits in the **feed**, where a connector's items stay until a person or an app keeps them in the library. It reads `read_only: true` because this connector carries no change back to the service: the next tutorial shows what happens to an edit made in Marfa.

</Step>
</Steps>
